post.title: A 401(k) takes over 3x what an IRA takes in 2026
post.ig:
A 401(k) takes over 3x what an IRA takes.

2026 limits: $24,500 for a 401(k) (+$8,000 at 50+, $11,250 at ages 60-63) vs $7,500 for an IRA (+$1,100 at 50+).
A 401(k) comes through your job, often with employer money (96% of Vanguard plans added some in 2025). An IRA you open yourself, with nearly any investment.
Example: $60,000 salary, 6% in = $3,600; a 50% match up to 6% adds $1,800.
Roth IRAs phase out at $153,000-$168,000 for single filers in 2026; Roth 401(k)s have no income limit. 2026 401(k) money must come out of paychecks by Dec 31; 2026 IRA money can go in until April 15, 2027.

Sources: IRS IR-2025-111 / Notice 2025-67 (Nov 2025); Vanguard How America Saves 2026.
News and education, not financial advice.

post.yt_desc:
For 2026, the 401(k) employee limit is $24,500 and the IRA limit is $7,500, per IRS Notice 2025-67. A 401(k) comes through your job and can include employer money (96% of Vanguard plans added some in 2025, per How America Saves 2026); an IRA you open yourself. Roth IRAs have income limits ($153,000-$168,000 phase-out for single filers in 2026); Roth 401(k)s don't. News and education, not financial advice.
